episode_title: Businesses as Advocates and Leaders in Society

real_qa.q: What is Business Declares and what are the three commitments required for member businesses?
real_qa.r: Business Declares is a not-for-profit network of about 140 progressive businesses focused on accelerating action to tackle climate, nature, and social justice crises. Membership is free, but businesses must make three commitments: they must declare publicly, advocate publicly, and publish a transition plan. The organization provides practical support through best practice sharing, future thinking via webinars, and direct action either as a network or supporting others' actions.

real_qa.q: What is the difference between Business Declares and B Corp certification?
real_qa.r: B Corp is an accreditation system where businesses must satisfy assessors across about five dimensions including climate and nature, then get scored and graded. Business Declares, by contrast, performs no accreditation because it operates with three directors, one paid employee, and volunteers, with no revenue. Business Declares focuses on helping businesses take bolder action and be part of a network that speaks out, lobbies, advocates, and shares truth-telling, emphasizing action and doing rather than proving and accrediting.
real_qa.requete: Business Declares vs B Corp differences

real_qa.q: How did Ben Tolhurst transition from JLL to founding Business Declares in 2019?
real_qa.r: In 2019, Ben Tolhurst experienced a climate epiphany when climate breakdown became mainstream, largely thanks to Extinction Rebellion. He realized he could not bring his whole self to work helping make money for clients who would be detrimental to his daughter's future. Having the privilege to do so, he quit his board-level role at JLL and helped co-set up Business Declares, driven by the personal question of whether he could look his children in the eye in 10 years and say he tried to do something about the crisis.
real_qa.requete: Ben Tolhurst JLL to Business Declares 2019

real_qa.q: What concrete actions does Business Declares recommend businesses take to address the polycrisis?
real_qa.r: Business Declares recommends actions ranging from tactical to strategic. Tactical actions include moving money away from banks like Barclays and HSBC (Europe's biggest funders of fossil fuel projects), speaking out, and signing petitions. More strategic actions include examining how crop failures will affect staff wages and living costs, future-proofing buildings against erratic weather, ensuring workers' homes are protected so they can come to work, and examining supply chains for issues like child labour in precious metal extraction for electric vehicles.
real_qa.requete: Business Declares actions fossil fuels climate

real_qa.q: How does Business Declares approach social justice issues like Black Lives Matter and Me Too within its member network?
real_qa.r: Business Declares does not prescribe a specific narrative on social justice issues but requires organizations to consider these matters thoughtfully. For issues like Black Lives Matter, Me Too, Gaza, and Ukraine, members must work through their own process: decide whether to speak out, understand why or why not, and produce something authentic. This approach recognizes that racial justice is deeply intertwined with climate breakdown, as examining the sourcing of precious metals in electric vehicles reveals connections to child labour and abusive systems.

guest.bio_context: Ben Tolhurst spent 25 years in corporate life, with his last role as board-level position at JLL (Jones Lang LaSalle) in the UK. In 2019, following a climate epiphany, he quit his position at JLL and co-founded Business Declares, a not-for-profit network of progressive businesses committed to addressing climate, nature, and social justice crises.
